faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.q1: Will you act as our importer of record?
faq.a1: No. We never act as importer of record. We audit your record and help you gather the information your broker asks for.
faq.q2: Do you file customs entries or CBP refund requests?
faq.a2: No. Your licensed customs broker prepares and files all customs entries and CBP refund requests.
faq.a3: No. Customer payments go straight to your account. We prepare payables; you approve them and release them from your own bank.
faq.q4: Whose name do collections run in?
faq.a4: Yours. Accounts more than 90 days late go to a licensed collection agency.
faq.a5: Collections calls run 8:00-16:00 US Eastern. We answer you in English or Turkish, and the first reply comes within 1 business day.
faq.a6: The check report arrives in 10 business days. A plan or desk starts once the engagement letter is signed.
faq.q7: Do we need to enter our tax ID on the site?
faq.a7: No. This site never asks for tax ID numbers, EINs or financial documents. Documents come through a secure channel after you sign.
faq.q8: Do you file export support claims?
faq.a8: No. Your support consultant at home files them in your government's system (for Türkiye, the Ministry of Trade's). We prepare the US-side documents and track the approvals and the payment.
faq.q9: Can Ponenti's fees be claimed as support?
faq.a9: No. Our fees are not an eligible cost. The support file is included in the flat monthly fee of the Standard and Complete plans.

result.lowBody: Your answers show no clear gap. Checking the rules once a year is still a good habit.

form5472Missing.title: Missing Form 5472 years
form5472Missing.body: The IRS penalty is $25,000 for each Form 5472 not filed, per year. If 90 days pass after an IRS notice, another $25,000 is added for each 30 days.

form5472Unknown.title: Form 5472 status unclear
form5472Unknown.body: Knowing which years were filed is the first step. Each missing year carries a $25,000 penalty.

iorAddress.title: Importer record address
iorAddress.body: Since September 18, 2026, CBP can void an importer number whose Form 5106 address is a registered agent, P.O. box or business center.

iorUnknown.title: Importer record unclear
iorUnknown.body: Without knowing who holds the record and what address it uses, you can't prepare for the new rules.

brokerCheck.title: No broker check yet
brokerCheck.body: Confirm with your broker that your record meets the new address rule. New importer requirements are being prepared under EO 14411.

salesTaxGap.title: Sales-tax gap
salesTaxGap.body: Since Wayfair (2018), a state can require you to collect its sales tax once your sales there pass its threshold, even with no physical presence. Each state you sell into without registering is a possible gap.

salesTaxUnknown.title: Sales-tax registrations unclear
salesTaxUnknown.body: Knowing where you are registered is the first step to closing gaps.

paymentDays.title: Long payment days
paymentDays.body: Every 10 days you cut from average payment days frees cash equal to about 2.7% of your annual US sales.

noFollowUp.title: No follow-up in US hours
noFollowUp.body: From Europe and the Middle East, the US East Coast is 5 to 8 hours behind. Without someone following up in US hours, payment questions wait until the next day.

refundBank.title: No bank account for CBP refunds
refundBank.body: CBP pays refunds only by ACH to a US bank account, and it holds IEEPA refunds for importers with no bank details on file in ACE.

refundUnknown.title: Refund account unclear
refundUnknown.body: Ask your broker whether ACH details are on file in ACE. Without them, refunds are held.

steps.title: The support file in four steps
steps.intro: Who does what, at every step.

s1.title: Setup
s1.body: We set up your US office or warehouse so it qualifies: an ownership link to your home company, a lease at market rent, and rent paid by bank transfer from the company or its US entity.
s1.who: Ponenti sets it up; you approve.

s2.title: Capture
s2.body: At every month-end close, each eligible cost is tagged in your books, with the invoice, proof of payment and bank statement attached.

s3.title: Approval
s3.body: We assemble the package for your government's commercial office in the US (for Türkiye, the Commercial Counselor) and track the site visit and the approval.
s3.who: Ponenti prepares it; the commercial office approves.

s4.title: Filing
s4.body: Your consultant at home files the claim in your government's system (for Türkiye, the Ministry of Trade's DYS), and we track it until it is paid.
s4.who: Your consultant files; we track it to payment.

estimator.title: Estimate your support
estimator.intro: For Türkiye's program, the first we cover. Enter your annual US costs: the estimate uses the 50% base rate and the rate of up to 70% that applies while the US is on the target-country list, in dollars and Turkish lira.

reasons.title: Why do US rent claims come back?
reasons.intro: Seven reasons, taken from the conditions of Türkiye's rent support. The support file checks each one before filing.
reasons.r1: Rent above market: the Commercial Counselor does not find it in line with market rates.
reasons.r2: Rent paid the wrong way: cash, a partner's personal account, a third party or a customer's check.
reasons.r4: Claim filed more than 6 months after the payment document date.
reasons.r5: No Turkish-made goods marketed at the site.
reasons.r6: Ownership that does not match the claim.
reasons.r7: Support above half of that year's exports to the US.
reasons.card: Paying by card is not by itself a reason for refusal. The circular then asks for the card statement, and the payment must still come from the company's account.
reasons.link: The seven reasons and the circular's articles (in Turkish)

lease.title: One lease, two problems
lease.p1: Since September 18, 2026, CBP can void an importer number whose Form 5106 address is a registered agent, P.O. box or business center. A real US office or warehouse solves that. The same lease, if it meets the conditions, can also qualify for rent support at home, such as Türkiye's unit rent support.
lease.p2: We help you find the space through licensed brokers and check the lease against both rules at once. A shared-office membership can qualify for rent support, but a business-center address can fail CBP's rule. So we never pick the address against one rule alone.

promise.title: If a claim comes back because of a document we prepared, we fix it at no charge.
promise.body: We correct the document and resubmit it, with no fee for it. The amount of support is your government's decision, so we show estimates, never promised amounts.

scope.i2: Ponenti's fees are not an eligible cost. Our fee is flat and does not depend on the amount of support.
scope.i3: Your support consultant at home files the claim and charges its own fee.
scope.i4: We share your records with your consultant only with your written consent.

notes.title: Data and definitions
notes.value: Value: general imports at customs value, in US dollars, excluding freight and insurance.
notes.window: Last 12 months: the latest 12 published months. Change compares them with the 12 months before.
notes.duty: Effective duty rate: the duty the Census Bureau calculates from customs entries, divided by the value of imports for consumption. Additional duties are included; later refunds and corrections are not.
notes.release: The Census Bureau publishes about five weeks after month end and revises past months each year with the April release.
notes.census: This product uses the Census Bureau Data API but is not endorsed or certified by the Census Bureau.

about.nameBody2: Ponenti carries companies west, to the United States. We started with Türkiye.
about.founderP1: I'm {name}. I grew up with Turkish and English, and I've spent my career in US finance and trade operations.
about.founderP2: I kept seeing companies from abroad, Turkish ones first, hit the same problems on the US side: filings run late, sales tax stays open in several states, US customers pay late, and follow-up happens by email from an office hours ahead.
about.founderP3: Ponenti exists to run that work at one desk, during US business hours, in English or Turkish.
about.bio: Bilingual in Turkish and English. Former UPS financial analyst and Senior Manager of Go-to-Market Strategy (pricing, revenue management, FP&A). Hands-on in bookkeeping and month-end close, B2B invoicing and collections, sales-tax filings, and customs entries with licensed brokers.
about.how1: Every client has one owner and a written deadline calendar.
about.how3: The numbers come from your own books: a cash report every week, a scorecard every quarter.
about.how4: Our limits are in writing: we're not your importer of record, we don't hold your money, and your broker files customs entries.
about.first10Intro: This is how the US back-office check runs.
about.step1: Intro call and document list. We ask for documents through a secure upload link, never as email attachments.
about.step2: Importer record: address, owners, bond and broker authorization. Filing history.
about.step3: Sales-tax exposure by state. Receivables aging and average payment days.
about.step4: Penalty exposure in dollars, a fix plan and a quote.
about.step5: Results call: the report, the priorities and the quote.
about.data2: The team: only the people assigned to your file. Before any access from outside the US, we get your signed Section 7216 consent.
about.data3: Return review and e-filing: a US accounting firm under contract.
about.data4: Software: business accounts with two-factor login. AI only on business plans that bar training.
about.data5: No one else: we don't sell your data or share it for marketing.
